chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the prayer upon the deceased, so he said: 'You exclaim five Takbeers. You say at the beginning of the first Takbeer: I testify that there is no God except Allah, Alone, there being no associates to Him, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad and upon the Imams of Guidance, and forgive us and our brethren who preceded us with faith, and do not make rancor in our hearts for those who believe. Our Lord, You are Gracious, Merciful. O Allah, forgive our living and our dead from the believing men and the believing women, and unite our hearts with the hearts of our good ones, and guide us to what we differ in, from the Truth, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to the Straight Path.'

So if the second Takbeer cuts off upon you, it will not harm you. You should say: O Allah, Your servant, son of Your servant, and son of Your maid. You are more knowing of him than I am. He is needy to Your Mercy and You are needless from him. O Allah, so overlook his sins and increase in his good deeds and forgive him and have mercy on him, and illuminate for him in his grave, and cause him to meet his Proof and his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and do not deprive us of his reward and do not try us after him.
You should say this until you finish the five Takbeers.

key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: His Proof (referring to the Imam or the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications and Takbeers recited during the funeral prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the Shia ritual prayer for the deceased, emphasizing the five Takbeers and specific supplications that reflect core theological concepts such as the intercession of the Prophet and the Imams. It highlights the practical application of mercy and forgiveness, linking the deceased's soul to the broader community of believers and ultimately to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The text underscores the Shia emphasis on precise recitation and the spiritual benefits of these prayers for both the dead and the living.
